summary.title: MemSlides: A Hierarchical Memory Driven Agent Framework for Personalized Slide Generation with Multi-turn Local Revision

details: Slide-generation agents produce polished decks but treat personalization as implicit prompt conditioning, so stable cross-session user preferences are not accumulated and multi-turn edits degrade into full-deck regeneration that overwrites already aligned content.

MemSlides: a presentation agent whose personalization is realized as an explicit memory hierarchy — long-term memory split into intent-conditioned user profile memory (what the deck should reflect, routed into the session at job start and consolidated back at job end) and tool memory (reusable execution experience at round and operation scope), plus session-scoped working memory carrying active preferences and edit state across revision rounds.

Scoped slide-local revision: each feedback turn is compiled into an explicit execution contract (Plan) fixing scope/targets/selectors, edits are applied as minimal selector- or rule-scoped patches on a local snapshot (Act), and completion is a checked state with snapshot-hash binding and coverage enforcement (Guard), so reading and writing stay local by construction.

10 occupation-style personas (e.g., postsecondary teacher, software developer, financial manager, legislator) × 3 role-intent buckets = 30 persona-intent profile entries used as read/write units of long-term memory.

Two-stage build: controlled authoring interactions over shared source material, then a seeded completion step (persona prompts + occupation-grounded role-preference registry) filling only empty theme/visual/layout/content/general fields with provenance tags; no synthetic interaction episodes or tool experiences created.
Three hosted model families: GPT-5, GLM-5, Gemini 3.1 Pro; all experiments are inference-time agent runs (no training), orchestrated locally with API-based generation and judging.

Baselines: DeepPresenter-style no-injection control (same source, model, persona, prompt and pipeline, but profile/session/tool memory withheld) and SlideTailor as an external reference/template-conditioned personalization system.

Persona-alignment judgments on complete round-0 decks: four 0–10 dimensions (Content, Structure, Visual, Specificity) with blind judging — judges see only persona summary and page-aligned rendered deck images under anonymous arm labels, with prompt, intent, system identity and memory condition hidden; three votes per dimension.
Structure deliberately excludes template-matching accuracy; Specificity uses distractor personas.

General-quality cross-check reusing DeepPresenter/PPTEval metrics: Constraint, Content, Style (1–5) and deck-level Diversity via DINOv2 embeddings with normalized Vendi score; Avg. = mean of the three 1–5 metrics.
Diagnostic matched-pair protocol: 9 pairs where source deck, model family, persona and modify request are fixed and only tool-memory injection varies; scenarios chosen before inspecting outcomes.

Trace-derived process metrics: Closed-Loop Completion (edit + verify + finalize), Strict Verify After Change (local verification within a short tool-call window), Time to First Correct Edit, and geometric-mean Core Tool Time Ratio excluding inspection and markdown-conversion calls.
Robustness: exact one-sided sign test over pair-level wins/losses; qualitative cases for working-memory delayed carryover (title color, summary-box style) and six-job cross-job profile consolidation.

key_findings.finding: Injecting intent-conditioned user profile memory yields broad round-0 persona-alignment gains over both a memoryless agent and a template-conditioned personalization system.
key_findings.evidence: Under blind persona-alignment judging, MemSlides wins all four dimensions against both baselines on GLM-5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro; averaged over the three model families it exceeds DeepPresenter by 1.37 (Content), 0.53 (Structure), 1.66 (Visual), 1.19 (Specificity) and SlideTailor by 2.73/2.95/2.79/3.08. On GPT-5, DeepPresenter retains a slight Structure edge, and per-persona GPT-5 results show +2.42 Overall on average across ten personas rather than a single-persona effect.

key_findings.finding: Tool-memory injection makes localized multi-turn editing more reliable and more search-efficient, without winning every matched pair.
key_findings.evidence: Across nine matched pairs, Closed-Loop Completion rises 0.815 to 0.963 (W-L-T-NA 3-1-5-0), Strict Verify 0.310 to 0.534 (8-1-0-0), Time to First Correct Edit falls 609.5s to 242.5s (6-2-0-1), and geometric-mean Core Tool Time Ratio is 0.327x (8-1-0-0); a one-sided sign test is strongest on Strict Verify and Core Tool Time Ratio, and core tool time totals 110.5s with memory vs 354.8s without.

key_findings.finding: The persona gains appear at the planning level (page roles, ordering, evidence emphasis) rather than being template-retrieval or generic polish effects.
key_findings.evidence: Structure improves jointly with Specificity even though the Structure rubric excludes template matching, Specificity is scored against distractor personas, and judges never see the original prompt, parsed intent, or system identity.

key_findings.finding: Improved persona alignment is not bought at the cost of ordinary presentation quality.
key_findings.evidence: On the same generated decks under DeepPresenter-style metrics, MemSlides attains the best Avg. on GPT-5 and GLM-5 and the best Style and Diversity on Gemini 3.1 Pro (though with lower Constraint there), and Content exceeds SlideTailor for all three model families.

key_findings.finding: Working memory and cross-job consolidation produce qualitatively visible preference carryover that a no-memory setting misses.
key_findings.evidence: Case studies show future-facing rules stated in an earlier turn (title color, summary-box style) being retrieved and applied only at the later triggering edit, and six repeated jobs where local feedback cues (evidence-boundary guardrails, owner/timeline closure tables, implementation checklists) reappear as default slide-organization patterns; qualitative comparison also shows DeepPresenter altering non-target slide regions where MemSlides patches only the requested element.
